sources.title: System Design Primer: Asynchronism, message queues, task queues and back pressure
sources.supportRationale: Required core conceptual/interview-study reference, inspected 2026-11-17; historical product comparisons are not adopted as current guarantees or evidence of question frequency.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1: Design and delivery semantics
sources.supportRationale: Partitioned storage, publication/consumption semantics and scoped transaction boundaries; examples explicitly target the 4.1 series rather than a latest-version claim.

sources.title: Kafka Java client 4.1.2: KafkaConsumer
sources.supportRationale: Position versus committed position, manual progress handling, rebalances, thread-safety and asynchronous processing caveats.

sources.title: Apache Kafka 4.1: Consumer configuration
sources.supportRationale: Classic group, poll/progress, isolation and bounded-fetch controls; protocol and settings are named rather than inferred from generic consumer terminology.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Queues
sources.supportRationale: Queue types, ordering and delivery lifecycle under the selected queue/consumer configuration.

sources.title: Amazon SQS: FIFO queues
sources.supportRationale: Per-group FIFO behavior and queue-mode distinctions in the service; client processing must honor the required order.

sources.title: Azure Architecture Center: Event Sourcing pattern
sources.supportRationale: Concurrency, snapshots, event evolution and projection rebuilding as separate design obligations.

sources.title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Transactional outbox
sources.supportRationale: Atomic local state/publication intent and remaining duplicate/consumer effect boundaries.

scenarios.theme: FIFO receipt still produces reversed account updates. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: One worker dispatches same-account records to concurrent tasks and update 42 commits before 41. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Serialize dependent work per account or enforce valid version transitions atomically at the sink

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Serial lanes reduce hot-key throughput

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: If operations truly commute, relaxing order may be valid, but that must be a domain property rather than an optimization assumption.

scenarios.theme: One customer owns most traffic. Will more workers fix ordering throughput?
scenarios.assumptions: All of that customer’s effects require serial execution in one ordered lane. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Message Ordering to hot key.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: One customer owns most traffic. Will more workers fix ordering throughput?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Measure the serial bottleneck, batch/optimize within the invariant and partition the business entity only if independent sub-invariants exist

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Stronger serialization caps throughput

scenarios.theme: New partitions reorder one account’s migration traffic. How do you prevent it?
scenarios.assumptions: Old work remains in the original lane while a changed mapping sends new work elsewhere. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: New partitions reorder one account’s migration traffic. How do you prevent it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Plan a coordinated mapping cutover/drain or enforce a supported entity sequence/ownership protocol at the effect boundary with gap handling

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Draining can pause writes and sequence enforcement adds state

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Partition order is local; it never promised order across two lanes.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to kdesign, kapi; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: A reassigned worker commits an older result after its replacement. What protects the sink?
scenarios.assumptions: The old process survives a rebalance and can still reach the database. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Message Ordering to stale worker.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A reassigned worker commits an older result after its replacement. What protects the sink?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use the selected store’s atomic version/ownership fencing mechanism and reject obsolete writes, while coordinating progress under the consumer protocol.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Fencing adds store checks and must cover the actual effect boundary

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A remote non-fenceable provider requires another idempotency/reconciliation contract; reassignment does not stop its earlier request.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to kapi, kconsumer, outbox; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.
